subject: AcmeCorp private offer — approval windows, term banding, and pricing bands
body:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@acme-corp.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sophie Martin <sophie.martin@acme-corp.com>, Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@amazon.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2027 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood private offer — term options + who needs to sign

Jordan,

Thanks for the demo last week. Acme procurement is ready to move on a Marketplace private offer but we need clarity on two things before we loop legal and finance:

- Term length options and how pricing changes across 12/24/36 month windows.
- Which internal approvers we need to pull in (finance vs procurement vs BU legal) to avoid delays — our buyer is multi-division.

Can you outline: pricing bands by annual commit, any minimums for co-sell credits, and an approval path that minimizes rework?

Attached is our standard procurement template for reference.

Thanks,
Liam
Procurement Manager
Acme Corporation
[Attachment: acme_procurement_template.pdf (pdf)]

---
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@amazon.com>, Sophie Martin <sophie.martin@acme-corp.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood private offer — term options + who needs to sign

Hi Liam —

Appreciate the template and the quick turnaround. High level answers below; I'll attach a pricing band matrix and a PO draft for your procurement team to review.

1) Term & pricing bands (typical):
- 12 months: baseline pricing (no term discount). Good for pilot and short evaluation.
- 24 months: ~12–18% aggregate discount vs 12m depending on commit bands. Helps lock predictable unit economics for both sides.
- 36 months: incremental discount beyond 24m but we generally limit to large enterprise deals; requires legal review for change-of-control and termination language.

Pricing bands are tiered by annual committed spend:
- <$250k/year: standard list
- $250k–$1M/year: mid-tier band (automated billing via Marketplace)
- >$1M/year: enterprise band (larger discount, reserved capacity options)

2) Approvals & who to loop:
- Procurement: required (PO issuance).
- Finance: required for multi-division chargeback or cross-BU deals — get them engaged early.
- Legal: only for >24 months or when custom SLRs/data clauses are requested.
- Sales ops / Revenue: required if you need early recognition changes.

3) Marketplace-specific notes:
- AWS private offers are signed in the console but buyer approval windows can vary by buyer org — seller-guided offers speed things up when buyer commits to the PO quickly.
- Co-sell credit eligibility typically requires a minimum contract value and that an AWS PM is onboarded during negotiation. I cc'd Priya for visibility.

Next steps: I'll send the pricing matrix + a PO draft (seller-side) for Acme to populate. If Acme prefers 24 months, we can show a 2-tier pricing band with a conservative reserved-capacity uplift.

Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[jordan_blake@redwood.ai]
[Attachment: pricing_band_matrix_20270816.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2027 12:22:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: ACME pricing band suggestion + approval thresholds

Looping Marcus + Laura for approval authority thresholds. A few operational points:

- I recommend we present a conservative 24-month option as the primary recommendation to Acme; it balances buyer budget cycles and our capacity planning.
- For deals where the customer requests >25% off list (or term >36 months), we need LAURA's signoff (legal + finance escalation).
- If Acme wants reserved capacity tied to the PO, we need to confirm region footprint (US-only vs multi-region) — this changes unit economics.

I've attached a quick pricing band matrix (workbook) that maps commit bands to suggested discounts and brief rationale lines per row. Please review.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood
[Attachment: pricing_band_matrix_20270816.xlsx (xlsx)]

---
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 17 Aug 2027 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME pricing band suggestion + approval thresholds

Quick note from infra/ops perspective:

- PO duration affects reserved capacity planning. A 24-month commit with a predictable monthly average allows us to offer better unit pricing because we can provision GPU pools accordingly.
- For co-sell credits, AWS requires an associated AWS PM and a co-sell plan in the pipeline — Priya, can you confirm the minimums on your side?
- If Acme is multi-region, we may need to size reserved capacity per-region which will raise the band slightly — call that a ~3–6% regional uplift depending on regions.

Linking the HubSpot deal for context: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/67890

Marcus Lin
Head of Infrastructure Partnerships, Redwood

---
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@acme-corp.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sophie Martin <sophie.martin@acme-corp.com>, Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@amazon.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Aug 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood private offer — term options + who needs to sign

Jordan —

Thanks, that table is helpful. Acme would prefer a 24-month term to align with our budgeting cadence. A couple asks:

1) Can you send a seller-side PO draft (we will populate our internal fields) and an ETA on how fast we can get the private offer into the AWS console once signatures are complete?
2) Our finance team needs a clear list of approvers — if you can specify titles (not just functions) we can map them to our internal org chart. For example: VP of Procurement, Director of Finance (Cloud), General Counsel (or delegated GC).
3) We have a procurement approval blackout the week of Aug 23 — any chance we can target getting signatures in by Aug 22?

Attached: Acme procurement template + internal approval flowchart.

Appreciate the help — we're aiming to close before their fiscal month end.

Liam
[Attachment: acme_internal_approval_flowchart.pdf (pdf)]

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@amazon.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Aug 2027 08:50:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood private offer — term options + who needs to sign

Liam —

Great — 24 months works for us and aligns with our recommendation. Attached is a seller-side PO draft (ACME_PO_DRAFT_v3.docx) populated with the 24-month pricing band placeholders. I've also added a short appendix that lists the typical approver titles we see on Acme-sized deals to make it easy for your mapping:

- VP, Procurement (issues PO)
- Director, Cloud Finance (approves chargeback and budget)
- General Counsel or Deputy GC (if >24 months or custom terms requested)
- Head of IT/Platform (technical acceptance for reserved capacity)

If you can share the names for those roles, we'll prepare the seller-guided private offer flow so we can move to the AWS console as soon as signatures are in. Typical timeline once signatures are complete: 1–3 business days to publish the private offer if buyer's AWS org is responsive; seller-guided offers can sometimes be same-day with the buyer liaison.

DocuSign link for initial signature routing (seller -> buyer): https://www.docusign.net/Acme-RDW-PO/Signing

Attachments: ACME_PO_DRAFT_v3.docx, pricing_band_matrix_20270816.xlsx, redwood-catalog-entry-screenshot.png

Next steps:
- Liam: confirm final approver names and whether Acme needs multi-region reservations (US-only vs US+EU).
- Sophie: if you can confirm internal budget owner and timeline, we'll aim to route for signatures by Aug 22.
- Priya: can you confirm co-sell eligibility with AWS PM notes?

Thanks all —

Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jordan_blake@redwood.ai
